subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Has small lines at the ends of strokes
Has no decorative strokes at the ends of letters
questions.explain: Sans-serif fonts lack the small finishing strokes (serifs) found on serif fonts.

questions.q: A serif font is one that has...
options: Small lines or 'feet' at the ends of letters
questions.explain: Serif fonts have small finishing strokes (serifs) at the ends of letters; sans-serif fonts do not.

questions.q: A 'storyboard' is most useful for planning...
options: A sequence such as an animation or advert
questions.explain: A storyboard sketches a sequence of frames to plan how an animation or film will unfold.

options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.
Kerning fine-tunes the spacing between specific pairs of letters for even, readable text.

questions.q: 'White space' (negative space) in a layout is...
options: A design fault to be avoided
The empty areas that help organise and balance a design
questions.explain: White space is the empty area around elements that gives a layout clarity and balance.

options: Arranging elements so the most important information stands out first
questions.explain: Visual hierarchy uses size, weight and position to guide the eye to the most important content first.

questions.q: 'Packaging' design must do all of these EXCEPT...
questions.explain: Packaging protects, informs and attracts, but it does not replace the product it contains.
Leading is the vertical spacing between lines of type, affecting readability.

questions.q: In graphic design, what does 'layout' mean?
options: The arrangement of text and images on a page
questions.explain: Layout is how text, images and space are arranged on the page or screen.

options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: A 'raster' (bitmap) image is made up of...
questions.explain: Raster images are built from a grid of pixels, so enlarging them too far makes them look blocky.

options: Ink that runs out of the cartridge
Artwork extended past the trim edge so no white border shows after cutting
questions.explain: Bleed extends the design beyond the trim line so trimming leaves no unwanted white edge.

options: Organise and align text and images consistently
questions.explain: A grid provides an underlying structure that keeps elements aligned and the layout consistent.

options: A drawn or painted image made to explain or decorate
A photograph taken with a camera
questions.explain: An illustration is a created image that supports, explains or decorates a piece of communication.

questions.q: Why is knowing the 'target audience' important in a design?
options: It has no effect on the design
It is only needed for sculpture
It shapes style, tone and content to suit who the design is for
It decides the price of paint
questions.explain: Understanding the target audience guides the style, language and imagery so the design appeals to them.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: RGB (red, green, blue) is the additive light model used by screens and digital devices.

options: A symbol or mark that identifies a brand
A full page of body text
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive symbol or wordmark used to identify and represent a brand.

questions.q: The CMYK colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, key/black) is the standard ink set used in colour printing.

options: Can only be black and white
Uses mathematical paths so it scales without losing quality
Is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged
questions.explain: Vector graphics use mathematical paths, so they can be scaled to any size without pixelation.

options: A trial version showing how a design will look
A finished printed product for sale
questions.explain: A mock-up is a realistic preview that shows how the final design will appear before production.

questions.q: A 'wordmark' (logotype) is a logo made from...
options: A stylised version of the brand's name in text
questions.explain: A wordmark is a logo formed from the company name set in distinctive, designed lettering.
